lines.trans: They look very much like you, Lev Egorych.
Just Lev, sweetheart, without the patronymic.
All right, Lyova, as you say.
I like your name very much.
Thank you very much for your kindness.
Then pour me another glass of wine.
Let us drink to our mutual happiness!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'wine glass, champagne flute, goblet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We'll drink from our wine glasses.
She raised a glass of champagne.

examples.text: Ничего страшного! Мы из наших бокалов выпьем.
examples.trans: No problem! We'll drink from our wine glasses.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

взрослый.gloss: adult, grown-up; (as a noun) a grown-up

meanings.note: as a noun, often plural: взрослые = grown-ups

examples.text: Маленькие умеют терпеть, а взрослые нет, понял?
examples.trans: Little ones can hold on, but grown-ups can't, got it?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

выпить.gloss: to drink, to have a drink

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: often used without an object for drinking alcohol

examples.trans: Oh, I've had a bit to drink now.
May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: + infinitive: давай убирать = let's clean up

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: + dative of person + accusative of gift

examples.text: Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?
We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

examples.text: Настоящий мужчина всегда оценит вашу доброту.
examples.trans: A real man will always appreciate your kindness.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

жалко.gloss: feel sorry for; it's a pity

meanings.note: impersonal predicate (+ dative of experiencer, + accusative/genitive)

examples.trans: I just feel sorry for him.

examples.text: Что за глупость? Эдик, мне его просто жалко.
examples.trans: What nonsense is that? Edik, I just feel sorry for him.
Edik, I just feel sorry for him.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: звать на помощь = to call for help
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...
Common neuter noun meaning 'name' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Let's find out the winner's name.

examples.text: Давайте узнаем имя нашего главного победителя!
examples.trans: Let's find out the name of our grand winner!

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
Just Lev, sweetheart, without the patronymic.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: налей мне чаю = pour me some tea; налей мужу = pour your husband a drink

examples.trans: Nina, pour your husband a drink. We've got something to celebrate!

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: the person who likes is in the dative: мне нравится = I like it

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.
This is a shared bathroom, Vanya!

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: traditional Russian naming derived from father's name

examples.trans: State your first name and patronymic.

examples.text: Зови меня просто по имени, без отчества.
examples.trans: Call me simply by first name, without patronymic.
Agreed, simply Lev, without a patronymic.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'present, gift' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a present for you.

examples.text: Это семейный праздник. Как в детстве, с подарками!
examples.trans: It's a family holiday. Like when we were kids, with presents!

meanings.note: usually short form похож/похожа/похожи + на + accusative

examples.trans: He looks very much like his father.

examples.text: Нормально у вас тут, просторно. И маскировка хорошая, на дворников похожи.
examples.trans: It's nice in here, roomy. And good disguises—you look like janitors.

meanings.note: Я прекрасно понимаю = I understand perfectly

examples.text: Нет, лучше так: все говорят, а я делаю! Прекрасно.
examples.trans: No, better like this: everyone talks, while I do! Excellent.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

examples.text: Он бы сейчас до потолка прыгал от радости.
examples.trans: He would be jumping to the ceiling for joy right now.
What a joy to see you!

examples.text: Мы с радостью сообщаем вам новость. Ваш долг полностью аннулирован!
examples.trans: We gladly inform you of the news. Your debt is completely canceled!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
Happiness is getting closer, almost here!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'son' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'довольствие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'pleasure' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Даже Лёша начал ходить в садик с удовольствием.
examples.trans: Even Lyosha started going to daycare with pleasure.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
